{{short description|Standard model of the structure of Earth's magnetic field}}
{{refimprove|date=June 2016}}
The '''International Geomagnetic Reference Field''' ('''IGRF''') is a standard mathematical description of the large-scale structure of the [[geomagnetism|Earth's main magnetic field]] and its [[geomagnetic secular variation|secular variation]]. It was created by fitting parameters of a mathematical model of the magnetic field to measured magnetic field data from surveys, observatories and satellites across the globe. The IGRF has been produced and updated under the direction of the [[International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy]] (IAGA) since 1965.<ref name="Thébault2015">{{cite journal |last1=Thébault|first1=Erwan |last2=Finlay|first2=Christopher C |last3=Beggan|first3=Ciarán D |last4=Alken|first4=Patrick |last5=Aubert|first5=Julien |last6=Barrois|first6=Olivier |last7=Bertrand|first7=Francois |last8=Bondar|first8=Tatiana |last9=Boness|first9=Axel |last10=Brocco|first10=Laura |last11=Canet|first11=Elisabeth |last12=Chambodut|first12=Aude |last13=Chulliat|first13=Arnaud |last14=Coïsson|first14=Pierdavide |last15=Civet|first15=François |last16=Du|first16=Aimin |last17=Fournier|first17=Alexandre |last18=Fratter|first18=Isabelle |last19=Gillet|first19=Nicolas |last20=Hamilton|first20=Brian |last21=Hamoudi|first21=Mohamed |last22=Hulot|first22=Gauthier |last23=Jager|first23=Thomas |last24=Korte|first24=Monika |last25=Kuang|first25=Weijia |last26=Lalanne|first26=Xavier |last27=Langlais|first27=Benoit |last28=Léger|first28=Jean-Michel |last29=Lesur|first29=Vincent |last30=Lowes|first30=Frank J |last31=Macmillan|first31=Susan |last32=Mandea|first32=Mioara |last33=Manoj|first33=Chandrasekharan |last34=Maus|first34=Stefan |last35=Olsen|first35=Nils |last36=Petrov|first36=Valeriy |last37=Ridley|first37=Victoria |last38=Rother|first38=Martin |last39=Sabaka|first39=Terence J |last40=Saturnino|first40=Diana |last41=Schachtschneider|first41=Reyko |last42=Sirol|first42=Olivier |last43=Tangborn|first43=Andrew |last44=Thomson|first44=Alan |last45=Tøffner-Clausen|first45=Lars |last46=Vigneron|first46=Pierre |last47=Wardinski|first47=Ingo |last48=Zvereva|first48=Tatiana |title=International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the 12th generation|journal=Earth, Planets and Space|date=27 May 2015|volume=67|issue=79|doi=10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9|doi-access=free|bibcode=2015EP&S...67...79T |url=https://hal-insu.archives-ouvertes.fr/insu-01412375/file/thebault-eps-2015-67.pdf}}</ref>

The IGRF model covers a significant time span, and so is useful for interpreting historical data. (This is unlike the [[World Magnetic Model]], which is intended for navigation in the next few years.)  It is updated at 5-year intervals, reflecting the most accurate measurements available at that time. The current 14th edition of the IGRF model (IGRF-14) was released in December 2024 and is valid from 1900 until 2030. For the interval from 1945 to 2020, it is "definitive" (a "DGRF"), meaning that future updates are unlikely to improve the model in any significant way.<ref name="Thébault2015" /><ref name=igrfhw>{{cite web |title=The International Geomagnetic Reference Field: A "Health" Warning |date=January 2010 |first=F.J. |last=Lowes |publisher=IAGA working group  V-MOD: Geomagnetic Field Modeling |url=https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/international-geomagnetic-reference-field/health-warning |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630025004/https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/IAGA/vmod/igrfhw.html |archive-date=2018-06-30 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Spherical Harmonics ==
The IGRF models the geomagnetic field <math>\vec{B}(r,\phi,\theta, t)</math> as a gradient of a [[magnetic scalar potential]] <math>V(r,\phi,\theta, t)</math>

:<math>
  \vec{B}(r,\phi,\theta, t) = -\nabla V(r,\phi,\theta, t) = -\left(\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial r}, \dfrac 1r\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial \theta}, \dfrac 1{r\sin \theta}\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial \phi}\right)
</math> 

The magnetic scalar potential model consists of the [[Gauss coefficient]]s which define a [[spherical harmonic]] expansion of <math>V</math><ref name="Thébault2015" />

:<math>
  V(r,\phi,\theta, t) = a \sum_{n = 1}^{N}\sum_{m=0}^n
  \left(\frac{a}{r}\right)^{n +1} \left(g_n  ^m (t)\cos m\phi + h_n  ^m(t)\sin m\phi\right) P_n  ^m\left(\cos\theta\right)
</math>

where <math>r</math> is radial distance from the Earth's center, <math>N</math> is the maximum degree of the expansion, <math>\phi</math> is East longitude,
<math>\theta</math> is colatitude (the polar angle), <math>a</math> is the Earth's radius,
<math>g_n^m</math> and <math>h_n^m</math> are Gauss coefficients, and <math>P_n^m\left(\cos\theta\right)</math>
are the Schmidt quasi-normalized [[associated Legendre function]]s of degree <math>n</math> and order <math>m</math>
:<math>
P_n^{m}(\cos\theta) = K_n\sin^{m} \theta\ \frac{d^{m+n}}{d(\cos\theta)^{m+n}}(\cos^2\theta-1)^n
</math>
where

:<math>
K_n = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2^n} & \text{; }m=0 \\ \frac{1}{2^n}\sqrt{\frac{2(n-m)!}{(n+m)!}} & \text{; }m>0 \end{cases}
</math>

is the normalization coefficient for the Schmidt quasi-normalized formulation.

The <math>(-1)^m</math> term usually present in the associated Legendre functions is omitted in this formulation and is instead accounted for in the Gauss coefficients.

The Gauss coefficients are modelled as a piecewise-linear function of time with a 5-year step size.<ref name="igrfhw" />
